_comment: Tough rock (prompt 09) and the layered underground. Every number is here; loaded once at startup. Metres = blocks. docs/tough.md.
_tough_note: off = T = 0 (prompt 08 exactly). layers off = pure sandstone below the surface (prompt 08 exactly)
_kind_override_note: null, 2 or 3: that kind on every rock column (testing). Kind 1 has no tough layer yet
_kind_map_note: mapped continent id (1 purple, 2 green, 3 blue, 4 brown, 5 red) -> kind. Ring and archipelago islands take the kind of the nearest mainland, scatter islands a seeded kind
_eligible_note: T = 0 where the base is under min_base above sand, within min_coast_distance of the coast, or where the local rock half-width is under min_halfwidth (bodies under 300 m across)
_mask_note: mesa mask value v from two noise scales; the plateau is v > threshold. The signed distance to the outline is s = (v - threshold) / |grad v| (metres, first order); the edge noise (metres) is added to s only within edge_fade of the outline, so the interior has no holes
_top_note: plateau top above sand = ref_scale x broad base reference + height (12..45, a noise at 600 m) + slow tilt + gentle undulation, at most max_top; the surface inside a mesa is max(base, top) so base summits may stand through it
_face_note: the cliff rises from the base to the top over (top - base) / slope metres, slope in blocks per column; ledges are a noise on the profile
_talus_note: an apron of base-coloured rock rises against the foot where a slow noise passes the gate (share of the cliff length); height from height_min to fraction x face height, over length metres
_bands_note: bands by height: a seeded sequence of palette blocks of 1..5 blocks, repeated every cycle_bands bands; the lookup height is shifted by two slow noises so bands are level within about 2 blocks over 100 m but differ between faces more than a kilometre apart. Cap: the top cap_depth blocks below the mesa top are red sandstone with terracotta patches
_underground_note: sandstone from the surface down to sand_level - depth (8..25 by a slow noise); then stone with ellipsoid blobs of other rock (about 10-20% of the stone); vanilla deepslate gradient y 8..0; vanilla bedrock floor
_kind2_note: kind 2 (plains, prompt 10): cliffs only on edges facing the weather direction (degrees from +X toward +Z, 90 = due south); the cliff weight is 1 within cone_full degrees of it and 0 beyond cone_zero. Eligibility is the same as kind 3 (the eligible block). Everything below is only read for kind 2; kind 3 is unchanged
_kind2_top_note: top above sand = ref_scale x broad reference + height (8..30 at the weather-side edge) - (plateau length to the weather side) / tilt_length + undulation, at most max_top. The length is a soft run of the mask along the weather direction (tilt_samples steps of tilt_step m), so the top dips by 1 block per tilt_length (40..80) m against the weather direction and has no fault
_kind2_fade_note: the eligibility limits (min_coast_distance, min_base, min_halfwidth) are soft for kind 2: the rise of the plain grows from 0 to its full value over this margin (metres of coast distance, metres of base reference, metres of half-width), so a limit makes a slope, not a wall
_kind2_ramp_note: ramp slope 1:slope_min..slope_max (metres per block, at its middle), eased at both ends by ease; cliff slope is blocks per metre of ground; the profile steepness is the logarithmic interpolation between the two by the cliff weight
_kind2_bands_note: kind 2 bands: the two palette colours alternate in 3..10 block bands, now and then a thin accent band; shifted by the same slow noises as kind 3. Cap: the top 1..3 blocks are red sandstone with patches of sandstone. No terracotta
